claims.text: Nanocrystalline transition-metal catalysts have a higher grain-boundary density than coarse-grained catalysts.
Nanocrystalline transition-metal catalysts will exhibit greater catalytic durability than compositionally identical coarse-grained catalysts.
Abundant grain boundaries promote rapid regeneration of catalytically active sites.
Grain boundaries limit the accumulation of deactivating defects through segregation and defect recombination.
Deposition and post-synthesis annealing can be adjusted to produce catalysts with nearly identical bulk compositions but different grain sizes.
Grain boundaries mediate the spatial distribution of catalytic active sites.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries promote localized defect recombination.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries limit catalyst poisoning.
Local lattice distortions in nanocrystalline catalysts create a rough energy landscape.
The rough energy landscape facilitates the mobility of defect species.
Enhanced defect mobility prevents defect clustering.
Grain boundaries act as sinks for deactivating defects and adsorbed poisons.
At grain boundaries, deactivating defects or adsorbed poisons recombine or desorb.
Removal of deactivating defects or poisons at grain boundaries regenerates active sites and sustains catalytic performance.
Under identical reaction conditions, the nanocrystalline catalyst will show lower activity decay over repeated cycles than the coarse-grained baseline.
The active surface area of the nanocrystalline catalyst will remain more constant during operation than that of the coarse-grained catalyst.
The proposed durability mechanism should cease to apply when reaction conditions cause rapid sintering or extensive morphological restructuring.
The proposed mechanism requires accessible grain boundaries that are not passivated by contaminants.
Analogous defect-dynamics behavior has been reported in radiation-resistance studies of high-entropy alloys.
A nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr high-entropy alloy showed no irradiation-created dislocation loops after irradiation to 8 dpa at 1073 K.
